title: Truth tables to Boolean networks
description: Build row detectors, verify all rows, simplify with a Karnaugh map and rebuild.
source_short: Lecture 2 / PDF pp.61-72 / original three-input example
source: Lecture 2 - Logistic Regression + Neural Network.pdf, pages 61-72. The three-input dataset is a study example.

pages.title: Start from a truth table
pages.subtitle: A small study example applying Lecture 2, pages 61-72; not the slide's five-input data.
blocks: Inputs A, B and C are Boolean. Output F must be 1 on exactly four input rows.
A literal is one input or its negation. NOT A means 1 - A for a Boolean input.

pages.title: Write one AND term per true row
pages.subtitle: DNF means an OR of AND terms. The bar over a letter means NOT.
blocks: Juxtaposed literals mean AND, not a new variable. A term tests all three bits; the final OR accepts any matching true row.

pages.title: Turn a row detector into a neuron
pages.subtitle: For row 001, all three matching literal values must be 1.
blocks: Three matches sum to 3 and give score +0.5. Any mismatch lowers that sum to at most 2, so the score is at most -0.5.
Negative weights encode the negated literals directly. No separate NOT neuron is needed.
We use H(s) = 1 when s >= 0. Half-integer thresholds avoid ties on Boolean inputs.

pages.title: The four hidden row detectors
pages.subtitle: Expand the complements in each matching-literal test in exactly the same way.
blocks: The output uses weights (1, 1, 1, 1) and threshold 0.5: at least one detector must fire.

pages.title: Work one row through every neuron
pages.subtitle: For input 001, only its own row detector should fire.

pages.title: Verify every canonical-network row
pages.subtitle: Scores are before H; hidden is the four-bit vector after H in detector order.
blocks: Detector order: 001, 011, 100, 101. A positive score becomes 1; every negative score becomes 0.
In each true row, hidden sums to 1 and output score is +0.5. In every false row, hidden sums to 0 and output score is -0.5.

pages.title: Arrange the same table as a K-map
pages.subtitle: Columns use Gray order: 00, 01, 11, 10. Adjacent columns differ by one bit.
blocks: Top pair 001/011: A = 0 and C = 1 stay fixed; B changes, so remove B.
Bottom pair 100/101: A = 1 and B = 0 stay fixed; C changes, so remove C.
Groups have power-of-two size. Adjacent edge cells may wrap around; diagonal cells are not adjacent.

pages.title: The reduced expression needs two detectors
pages.subtitle: Grouping removed tests whose input can change without changing the output.
blocks: h1 ignores B; h2 ignores C. Each detector now checks two literals rather than three.
This reduces the number of hidden neurons from four to two without changing the truth table.

pages.title: Verify reduced network: rows 1-2
pages.subtitle: Substitute inputs, threshold both hidden scores, then threshold their sum.

pages.title: Verify reduced network: rows 3-4
pages.subtitle: Substitute inputs, threshold both hidden scores, then threshold their sum.

pages.title: Verify reduced network: rows 5-6
pages.subtitle: Substitute inputs, threshold both hidden scores, then threshold their sum.

pages.title: Verify reduced network: rows 7-8
pages.subtitle: Substitute inputs, threshold both hidden scores, then threshold their sum.

pages.title: Count what the simplification saved
pages.subtitle: A stored zero weight still counts as a parameter of a dense layer.
blocks: Four hidden neurons each have three input weights and a bias; the output has four weights and one bias.
The sparse version omits the unused B-to-h1 and C-to-h2 edges: six present weights plus three biases. Counts depend on how connections are stored.

pages.title: Your turn: a different truth table
pages.subtitle: Set F = 1 for 010, 011, 101 and 111; set F = 0 elsewhere.
blocks: 1. Place all eight rows into a K-map with columns BC = 00, 01, 11, 10.
2. Group adjacent ones and write a reduced OR-of-ANDs expression.
3. Convert each term into a hidden neuron, then add an OR output.
4. Check all eight rows against the requested truth table.
Use the same H convention and half-integer thresholds.

pages.title: Practice answer: group and translate
pages.subtitle: Each group removes the input that changes inside that group.
blocks: Top pair 010/011 keeps A = 0, B = 1: NOT A AND B. Bottom pair 101/111 keeps A = 1, C = 1: A AND C.

pages.title: Practice answer: all eight rows
pages.subtitle: The output applies H(h1 + h2 - 0.5) to each row.
blocks: Avoid: ordinary binary column order in the map; diagonal grouping; forgetting to adjust the bias when expanding NOT literals.
